title: slicer tui: O leads the Roadmap hint; drop a stale cursor restore; share the O condition
lead: *Proposed.* `O slicer tui` is the first entry of the Roadmap hint. After slicer's TUI exits, ork restores the Roadmap cursor only from a project read that started after the exit, drops the restore on an item-list error or when the owner moves the cursor first, and the help line and the `O` refusal share one availability helper.
findings_note: 2026-11-17 spec draft of S231 (S69 items 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 and 7; adj 440) at f48a6154. `O slicer tui` is added after the row actions and before `m matrix` (`internal/tui/keys.go:534-555`; pinned at `internal/tui/slicertui_test.go:158,275,281`). `restoreSlicerTuiCursor` keeps the restore on an item-list error and never drops it when the owner moves (`internal/tui/slicertui.go:71-91`); a coalesced return uses the in-flight reply (`internal/tui/model.go:404-409`, `:342-356`); the help condition repeats `slicerTuiRefusal` (`internal/tui/view.go:868`, `internal/tui/slicertui.go:26-41`).

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
Owner decisions (2026-11-17): adj 440 (Q5), `O slicer tui` moves to the first position in the Roadmap hint. adj 439 (Q4, scrollable help) is the separate slice "Scrollable help overlay" below, which also touches `internal/tui/view.go:860-900`, so it runs after this one.

From S231, later notes of S69 (pair wave 2, 2026-11-01), re-checked at HEAD f48a6154:

- S69 item 1, still present. `restoreSlicerTuiCursor` returns early, keeping `m.slicerTuiRestore`, when the snapshot has `Items.Err` (`internal/tui/slicertui.go:74-77`). Nothing else clears it (`rg -n slicerTuiRestore internal/tui` finds only `model.go:158,405` and `slicertui.go:74,78`), so a later good read can move a cursor the owner has moved since.
- S69 item 2, still present. `testSlicerTuiReturn` switches project before the return but sends no selection and checks only the reads (`internal/tui/slicertui_test.go:114-143`); no test checks the cursor when the restore's project is not the active one (`slicertui.go:79-81`).
- S69 item 3, still present. On return ork calls `m.fetch(project, true)` (`internal/tui/model.go:409`); when a read is in flight, `fetch` returns nil (`model.go:344`) and the in-flight reply, read before slicer wrote, consumes the restore (`model.go:1287`). The test `TestSlicerTuiReturnFollowsTheSelectedItemAfterRefresh` (`slicertui_test.go:188-232`) sets the new list before it runs the pending read, so it does not show this. The daemon refresh asked for on return is also skipped then (`model.go:350-353`).
- S69 item 4, still present. The help line computes `slicerTui := m.itemPane == nil && m.active >= 0 && loaded && !Unavailable && !setup()` (`internal/tui/view.go:868`), a copy of part of `slicerTuiRefusal` (`slicertui.go:26-41`).
- S69 item 7 (O placement), changed by the owner (adj 440). Today the hint adds `enter open` and `l launch` (`internal/tui/keys.go:536`), then `P`, `J/K`, then `O slicer tui` (`keys.go:553-554`) and `m matrix`; the wide hint reads `N note; enter open; l launch; O slicer tui; m matrix` (`internal/tui/slicertui_test.go:158`), and `docs/dashboard.md:2167-2169` says O follows the row actions. The drop tier of O (`dropSlicerTui`, `keys.go:211`) is not part of the decision and stays.
- S69 item 6 (human check to add), still present: no [HUMAN CHECK] covers a resize while slicer's TUI is open or a ctrl+c exit (`docs/dashboard.md:2148-2160` describes only the normal and failed exits).

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
All tests are in `internal/tui/slicertui_test.go`, using slicerTuiHarness. Anchors checked against the initial worktree; named symbols take precedence after edits.

- `TestHintBarOffersSlicerTuiOnTheRoadmap` (:152-186): wideHint starts O slicer tui; remaining row actions keep their order. Existing 80x24 and 100x30 checks continue to hide O at its unchanged drop tier.
- `TestSlicerTuiHintFollowsRowActionsWhenEditHintsAreHidden` (:268-284), renamed `TestSlicerTuiLeadsTheRoadmapHint`: without daemon prefix O slicer tui; enter open; tab views; empty list prefix O slicer tui; l launch; m matrix. Red: O follows row actions.
- `TestSlicerTuiRestoreIsDroppedOnAnItemListError`: failed item read consumes restore; later good read after j leaves cursor 1. Red: cursor moves to 2.
- `TestSlicerTuiRestoreIsDroppedWhenTheCursorMoves`: j before refresh leaves cursor 1. Red: restore moves it to 2.
- `TestSlicerTuiReturnToAnotherProjectLeavesItsCursor`: other project cursor 1 is untouched, restore consumed, switching back resets cursor to 0. Passes on arrival; regression pin.
- `TestSlicerTuiReturnSkipsAReadStartedBeforeTheExit`: replaces in-flight branch in `TestSlicerTuiReturnFollowsTheSelectedItemAfterRefresh` (:188-232); stale reply leaves cursor and restore pending, follow-up fresh read moves S90 to row 2 and requests one daemon refresh. Red: stale reply consumes restore, no follow-up.
- `TestSlicerTuiHelpAndRefusalAgree`: unloaded, unavailable, setup, item pane, matrix pane and ready states agree between help and refusal. Passes on arrival; regression pin.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Write the failing tests above and see them red for the stated reason.
2. `keys.go`: add the `O slicer tui` entry first in the Roadmap hint (`keys.go:511`, before `n new slice`), keeping its drop tier `dropSlicerTui`; the item-pane branch is unaffected because O is refused there.
3. `slicertui.go`: add a helper, for example `slicerTuiProjectReady()`, for the project part (active, loaded, available, not in setup). `slicerTuiRefusal` and the help condition in `view.go:868` both call it; the help keeps its `m.itemPane == nil` check.
4. `slicerTuiSelection`: record the cursor at return (`atReturn`) and whether a read was in flight then (`skipOne`). On the done message: when `m.poller.InFlight(project)`, set `skipOne` and mark the project for a follow-up read that asks the daemon to refresh (extend the `dirty` follow-up at `model.go:1298-1301` with a refresh flag, or an equivalent).
5. `restoreSlicerTuiCursor`: if `skipOne`, clear it and return. On `Items.Err`, drop the restore. If the project is active on the Roadmap and the cursor is not `atReturn`, drop the restore without moving the cursor. Keep the existing item-follow and clamp rules.
6. Run `go test ./internal/tui -update` only if a golden's hint shows `O slicer tui`, and review the diff.
7. Docs: `docs/dashboard.md:2157`: the restore waits for a read that starts after slicer's TUI exits, and is dropped on an item-list error or when the cursor moved first. `docs/dashboard.md:2167-2173`: `O slicer tui` leads the Roadmap hint (adj 440), with the two example hints rewritten. CHANGELOG.md: one bullet at the end of `## Unreleased`.
8. UI slice: UI pass (r14).

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
Acceptance criteria:

- On a screen wide enough for every hint, the Roadmap hint starts 'O slicer tui;'.
- After slicer's TUI exits with an item-list error, a later good read does not move the cursor.
- Moving the cursor before the refreshed list arrives cancels the restore.
- Returning while another project is active leaves that project's cursor, pinned by a test.
- A read in flight at the exit does not consume the restore; the read after it does, with a daemon refresh.
- The help line and the 'O' key agree on when 'O slicer tui' is offered.
- The two human checks below are run and their results recorded.

Commands:

- `go vet ./...` exits 0.
- `go test ./...` exits 0.
- `go test ./internal/tui -run 'SlicerTui' -v` lists the new tests as passing.
- `gofmt -l .` prints nothing.
- `slicer check` exits 0.
- `adj lint` exits 0.
- `rg -n 'm.projects\[m.active\].loaded && !m.projects\[m.active\].snap.Unavailable' internal/tui/view.go` prints nothing.
- `go test ./internal/tui -run 'HintBarOffersSlicerTui|SlicerTuiLeadsTheRoadmapHint' -v` passes.
- [HUMAN CHECK] In a 200x40 terminal, open the Roadmap: the hint line starts `O slicer tui;`. At 100x30 and 80x24 the hint line does not show it (unchanged drop tier).
- [HUMAN CHECK] In a 100x30 terminal, open the Roadmap, select the third item, press `O`; inside slicer's TUI resize the terminal to 80x24, then quit it normally: ork redraws at 80x24 with the cursor on the same item and no stale lines.
- [HUMAN CHECK] In a 100x30 terminal, press `O` on the Roadmap, then quit slicer's TUI with ctrl+c: record whether the status line shows `slicer tui: exit status N` (and which N), and that ork stays responsive.
